newsitem.title: USA: NYMEX Hub natgas slips late despite firmer cash.
newsitem.headline: NYMEX Hub natgas slips late despite firmer cash.

text.p: NYMEX Henry Hub natgas futures mostly lost ground late Wednesday in moderate trade despite firmer physical prices, hit by some technical selling when an early rally attempt stalled at resistance, sources said.
At 1420 EDT, August eased 1.1 cents to $2.105 per million British thermal units, while September was down the same at $2.115. Most other deferreds were down by 0.3 to 1.2 cents.

"I think we got to $2.14 (in August) on the Transco situation, but I continue to believe every rally will be sold harder. People are waiting to sell rallies," said one Texas trader, adding he expected August to break below $2 soon.
He said reports last night of a gas leak on an offshore Louisiana Transco pipeline spurred some buying on ACCESS, but sellers surfaced this morning on news the line had quickly been repaired.
With warmer weather forecast for the Midwest and East later this week and next, some expected physical prices to stay buoyant and paper to move up to close the gap.
"Cash has been steady to firm and they haven't been able to bust it. I think the next move in futures is higher," said one East Coast trader.

Chart traders also saw a more positive technical picture after yesterday's reversal, but most agreed August needed to close today in positive territory to confirm the signal. They pegged August support at Tuesday's low of $2.051, with psychological support seen at $2. Resistance was at $2.15 and then along the down trendline at $2.25.
A Reuter poll this week showed most expected a weekly AGA stock build of 83-88 bcf when the report is released later today. For the same week last year, stocks rose by 90 bcf.
In the cash Wednesday, Gulf Coast prices firmed two cents to the low-to-mid teens. Midcon pipes were about three cents higher in the low-$2s. New York city gate gas was unchanged in the high-$2.30s.
NYMEX said 21,201 contracts traded at 1350 EDT.
On the KCBT, August slipped one-half cent to $2.00, while deferreds were still steady to one cent lower. The East/West spread narrowed by 0.6 cent to 10.5 cents (NYMEX premium).
